title: Demons, as the Fallen see them
summary: What the word demon means among the Nephandi.

claims.text: Here demon means an Otherworldly being with built-in hostile aims, not only a Fallen Angel in the Christian sense.
The Greek daimon once meant a spirit, even a helpful muse, and the Sanskrit deva named shining good beings; the darker sense grew as Christianity spread.
The Fallen use the word for higher beings that humanity has cursed and spurned, and that resent humankind in return.

title: Abyssal Litanies
summary: The written and spoken lore of the Nephandi.

claims.text: The Litanies gather legends, rites, spells, histories and debates, giving the Fallen a shared identity.
The Heralds of Basilisk keep online archives where Litanies are gathered, translated and annotated, though no one can test how true they are.
Litanies often blend several tongues at once, Arabic, Latin, Greek, Sanskrit and English among the most common, with cuneiform and others besides.

title: Barabbi and the Fallen Disparates
summary: Mages who turn from other factions to the Nephandi.

claims.text: Barabbi are Nephandi who began in other groups, and many of them started out among the Nine Traditions.
Ambition, desperation, pride and revenge draw Disparates and unaligned mages toward the Cauls, since looser sects offer more freedom and more chances to Fall.
The Disparate Alliance was formed in theory to fight the Nephandi, so it may punish Nephandic ties more harshly than any other faction.

title: Widderslainte
summary: People reborn with a Nephandic Avatar.

claims.text: A widderslainte is a newborn whose Avatar was already Nephandic, a soul that keeps pushing its new life back toward the Fallen.
Theories call such souls escaped Nephandi returning from the hells, alien minds, demonic urges or broken Avatar shards.
A widderslainte child is not held to be a Nephandus, since a child lacks adult judgment, but one at grave risk of becoming one.

title: Infernalists, K'llashaa and Malfeans
summary: The three classic faces of the Fallen.

claims.text: To most mages these three sects stand for all Nephandi, a view that is badly mistaken.
Infernalists are a cluster of demon-dealing cults and serve as the best-known face of the Fallen, though today many of them are unAwakened hangers-on.
Infernalists take old Nephandic titles in earnest; Sleeper members stay as servants and fodder unless they prove more useful, while Night-Folk allies rank far higher.
Malfeans hold that life is a lie and that decay and collapse are the last truth of the Void.

title: The Qlippoth
summary: The dark mirror of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.

claims.text: Where a Kabbalist climbs the Tree of Life toward God, a Qlippothic mystic descends through broken shells to become a god.
The Qlippoth runs from Lilith, mother of demons, to Thaumiel, godhood through annihilation, beyond which occult lore speaks of a Black Diamond or Universe B.
Daath, the Abyss or Door to Knowledge, is met twice on the Nephandic path: once in the Caul and again before the last three shells; few pass the second time.

title: Cauls
summary: The gateways through which mages Fall.

claims.text: Inside a Caul there is no time or distance; the mage is unmade by the Abyss and comes out remade as a vessel of the Void.
Nephandi call Cauls anti-Nodes, Flowers of Rebirth, fruits of Hell or alien beings; their true nature is unknown.
Mages cannot make a Caul alone, so the Fallen usually build their lairs around one that already exists.
Physical disasters can harm a Caul's outer form, but that damage heals over time.
